Question:
Can we still use the 50-hour allowance in AD 2013-11-11 when a switch reaches 3,000 hours?

Source: TRAIN-AD, section 4
The engine oil pressure switch
P/N 83278, 3,000 hours Replace with a new, zero-time switch Record part number, date, and airframe hours
Speaker notes: The 50-hour allowance in paragraph (g)(6) of AD 2013-11-11 applied once, to switches that were already at or near the limit when the directive took effect on 1 August 2013. It is not a grace period you can use today. Our manual, section 3.2, applies the same 3,000-hour limit to every 172R and 172S we maintain.

Source: PROC-R7, section 3
3.1 Tracking. Time-controlled parts are listed in the fleet register, sheet Time-controlled parts, with the airframe hours at installation. The hours used on a part are the airframe's current total time minus the airframe hours at installation.

3.2 Engine oil pressure switch. AD 2013-11-11 limits the engine oil pressure switch, P/N 83278, to 3,000 hours time-in-service on the airplanes within its applicability. Anfa applies the same 3,000-hour limit to every Cessna 172R and 172S it maintains, including those outside the directive's serial number ranges. Plan the replacement when a switch reaches 2,900 hours. Keep two switches in stock.

3.3 When the records disagree. If the fleet register and a work order or logbook give different hours for the same installation, use the lower airframe hours at installation until the quality manager has resolved the difference. Never use the figure that gives the part more time.

Source: AD-2013-11-11, section 
If after the inspection required in paragraph (g)(1) of this AD it is confirmed that P/N 83278 engine oil pressure switch is installed, through inspection of the airplane or engine logbooks determine the TIS of the engine oil pressure switch.

If after the inspection required in paragraph (g)(1) of this AD you cannot positively identify the hours TIS on the P/N 83278 engine oil pressure switch, before further flight, replace the engine oil pressure switch with a new, zero time, P/N 83278 engine oil pressure switch. Record the engine oil pressure switch part number, date, and airplane hours in the airplane log book. The recorded engine oil pressure switch TIS will be used as the benchmark for calculation of the 3,000 hour TIS limit on the engine oil pressure switch.

(6) When the engine oil pressure switch is at or greater than 3,000 hours TIS or within 50 hours TIS after August 1, 2013 (the effective date of this AD), whichever occurs later, and repetitively thereafter at intervals not to exceed 3,000 hours TIS on the P/N


Source: AD-2013-11-11, section 
04-01 applies to the specified products. The SNPRM published in the Federal Register on March 7, 2013 (78 FR 14726). The NPRM (77 FR 60062, October 2, 2012) proposed to increase the applicability of the AD and place a life-limit of 3,000 hours time-in-service (TIS) on the engine oil pressure switch, requiring replacement when the engine oil pressure switch reaches its life limit. The SNPRM proposed to change the applicable serial numbers ranges and place a life-limit of 3,000 hours TIS on the engine oil pressure switch, requiring replacement when the engine oil pressure switch reaches its life limit.

Source: AD-2013-11-11, section 
AGENCY: Federal Aviation

Administration (FAA), DOT.

ACTION: Final rule.

SUMMARY: We are superseding AD 2000-04-01 that applies to certain Cessna Aircraft Company (Cessna) Models 172R, 172S, 182S, 182T, T182T, 206H, and T206H airplanes. AD 2000-04-01 currently requires an inspection of the engine oil pressure switch and, if applicable, replacement of the engine oil pressure switch. This AD increases the applicability of the AD, places a lifelimit of 3,000 hours time-in-service on the engine oil pressure switch, and requires replacement when the engine oil pressure switch reaches its life limit. This AD was prompted by new reports of internal failure of the engine oil pressure switch, which could result in complete loss of engine oil with consequent partial or complete loss of engine power or fire. We are issuing this AD to correct the unsafe condition on these products.

DATES: This AD is effective August 1, 2013.

The Director of the Federal Register approved the incorporation by reference of certain publications listed in the AD as of August 1, 2013.

message.content:
No, the 50-hour allowance in AD 2013-11-11 cannot be used today. According to the training material, that allowance "applied once, to switches that were already at or near the limit when the directive took effect on 1 August 2013. It is not a grace period you can use today." The AD text itself ties the 50-hour window to the effective date of August 1, 2013 ("within 50 hours TIS after August 1, 2013"), and the current maintenance manual applies a strict 3,000-hour limit with replacement planning at 2,900 hours.

Source: TRAIN-AD, section 4 (speaker notes); AD-2013-11-11, section (paragraph (g)(6)); PROC-R7, section 3.2
message.reasoning:
The user is asking whether the 50-hour allowance in AD 2013-11-11 can still be used when a switch reaches 3,000 hours. I need to check the provided passages for the answer.

Looking at the sources:

1. TRAIN-AD, section 4: Contains speaker notes that explicitly state: "The 50-hour allowance in paragraph (g)(6) of AD 2013-11-11 applied once, to switches that were already at or near the limit when the directive took effect on 1 August 2013. It is not a grace period you can use today."

2. PROC-R7, section 3: Section 3.2 states: "AD 2013-11-11 limits the engine oil pressure switch, P/N 83278, to 3,000 hours time-in-service on the airplanes within its applicability. Anfa applies the same 3,000-hour limit to every Cessna 172R and 172S it maintains, including those outside the directive's serial number ranges. Plan the replacement when a switch reaches 2,900 hours. Keep two switches in stock." No mention of a 50-hour allowance for current use.

3. AD-2013-11-11, section: Contains paragraph (g)(6) which says: "When the engine oil pressure switch is at or greater than 3,000 hours TIS or within 50 hours TIS after August 1, 2013 (the effective date of this AD), whichever occurs later, and repetitively thereafter at intervals not to exceed 3,000 hours TIS on the P/N..." This shows the 50-hour allowance was specifically tied to the effective date of August 1, 2013.

4. AD-2013-11-11, section: Background information about the AD.

5. AD-2013-11-11, section: Header information showing effective date August 1, 2013.

The TRAIN-AD speaker notes directly answer the question: the 50-hour allowance applied once to switches at or near the limit when the directive took effect on August 1, 2013, and is not a grace period that can be used today. The AD text itself shows the allowance was for switches "within 50 hours TIS after August 1, 2013."

So the answer is no, we cannot still use the 50-hour allowance today. It was a one-time provision for the effective date of the AD.
